shots.line: Your front door has one peephole.
shots.scene: Front view of the inner face of the front door in the dark entry: one gray peephole lens glowing with hallway light, handle and deadbolt, light leaking under the door.
shots.purpose: Establish the normal door, readable at phone size.
shots.visual_change: Static door with one lit lens; a yellow ring pulses around it on 'one'.

shots.line: If you come home and there are
shots.scene: Side cutaway: the person, outside in the hallway, unlocks; the door opens on 'come'; they step in; the door shuts behind them; they turn to face it.
shots.purpose: Show arriving home in the recurring stage.
shots.visual_change: Unlock reach -> door open (2.85) -> walk in -> door shut (3.80) -> turn.

shots.line: two…
shots.scene: Same front view of the door, just shut: a second lens with a brass ring opens above the old one.
shots.purpose: Make the impossible second peephole unmistakable without labels.
shots.visual_change: Door settles from the slam; at 0.1 s a brass lens grows above the old lens with a yellow pulse.

shots.line: don't use the NEW one.
shots.scene: Rule card: RULE 1 / DON'T USE THE NEW ONE with a four-step progress row.
shots.purpose: State the protocol rule on the turn.
shots.visual_change: Hard cut from the room to the rule title; rule 1 of 4 is lit.

shots.line: The old one lets the hallway light in. The new one stays dark.
shots.scene: Frontal insert of the inner door face: brass NEW lens above the gray OLD lens. The old glass glows warm with light rays; the new glass is pure black.
shots.purpose: Make the contradiction readable at phone size.
shots.visual_change: OLD label -> glow and rays swell with a green check on 'light' -> NEW label -> red ring and red cross on 'dark'.

shots.line: Through the old one, the
shots.scene: Back in the same cutaway. The person crosses to the door and presses an eye to the OLD peephole; their head blocks the beam and the floor spot disappears.
shots.purpose: Show the rule being followed with a visible contact beat.
shots.visual_change: Stand -> walk -> lean into the peer pose; contact with the old hole at about 0.9 s blocks the light.

shots.line: hallway is empty.
shots.scene: Fisheye POV through the old peephole: bowed hallway, neighbour door 4D, the same wall sconce. Nobody is there.
shots.purpose: Answer what the person sees; confirm the hallway is empty.
shots.visual_change: Lens view drifts slightly; a green check and NO ONE OUTSIDE status confirm 'empty'.

shots.line: So why is the new one still dark?
shots.scene: Extreme close-up of the brass NEW lens with black glass on the door face. A slow push-in. In the narration pause, the black glass blinks: a lid closes and reopens, and a catchlight appears.
shots.purpose: Reveal the impossible answer without words.
shots.visual_change: Static black lens with a glass reflection -> blink at 2.65 s -> eye catchlight and iris; status NO LIGHT -> NOT A LENS.

shots.line: It isn't there for you to look out. It's there for something to look IN.
shots.scene: Same cutaway. The person pulls back from the door and backs across the room. A dotted sight-line grows from the NEW hole and tracks their head. On 'IN' it turns red and locks on. The old hole's floor light then goes out too.
shots.purpose: Payoff and escalation: the new hole watches in; final callback to the floor light spot.
shots.visual_change: Peer -> recoil -> backing away; yellow sight-line grows and follows; red lock with WATCHED on 'IN'; at 5.6 s the old beam and floor spot fade out.

shots.line: Rule two.
shots.scene: Rule card: RULE 2 / SIT AGAINST THE DOOR, progress 2 of 4.
shots.purpose: State rule two.
shots.visual_change: Hard cut to the card; rule 2 lit.

shots.line: If both are dark,
shots.scene: Insert of the inner door face: both lenses black, the old one no longer lit. Thin red rings on 'dark'.
shots.purpose: Show that both are dark.
shots.visual_change: Static both-dark lenses; red rings on 'dark'.

shots.line: sit with your back against the door. You can't see out anymore.
shots.scene: Side cutaway: the person walks from mid-room to the door under a red lock from the new hole, turns and slides down to sit with their back to the door. The lock breaks as they get under it.
shots.purpose: Demonstrate the rule's action.
shots.visual_change: Walk -> turn -> sit; red locked line -> yellow lost line fading.

shots.line: But it can't see everything, either.
shots.scene: Extreme close-up of the brass new lens, now an eye: the iris and catchlight dart left, right and down, searching.
shots.purpose: A searching lens: the threat is active but blind to part of the room.
shots.visual_change: Eye looks left (0.25), right (1.05), down-left (1.8).

shots.line: A peephole only looks one way. In, and a little down. So there's one place it can't reach: right underneath it.
shots.scene: Diagram over the held room: red view cones grow from both holes, then tilt down to their limit. The triangle under the door, where the person sits, fills green and is labelled BLIND SPOT with a check.
shots.purpose: Explain why the rule works with visible geometry.
shots.visual_change: No overlay -> cones on 'one way' -> cones tilt 'a little down' -> green blind spot and check on 'underneath'.

shots.line: Sit there. Back flat to the door. Don't get up until morning.
shots.scene: Medium close (2x) on the seated person at the door: they press their back flat against the door, then brace a hand on the floor.
shots.purpose: Show survival as small physical actions, not captions.
shots.visual_change: Back presses flat (43.0) with contact marks; hand plants on the floor (44.7-45.1) with a small tap.

shots.line: It will look for you. At the table. At the picture. At the spot where the light used to be.
shots.scene: Wide: a narrow yellow search beam from the new hole lands on the table, then the picture, then the dashed place where the floor light used to be. Each target flashes. It never reaches the door.
shots.purpose: The threat searches the familiar room; the blind spot holds.
shots.visual_change: Beam appears; table glow (1.71), picture glow (2.75), spot outline (3.87).

shots.line: Let it look.
shots.scene: Medium close: a red beam from the old hole sweeps down to its limit and grazes just over the tucked head, holds, then withdraws.
shots.purpose: Near miss: suspense inside a quiet hold.
shots.visual_change: Beam angle 12 -> 41 degrees (0.3-1.0); the head tucks (0.5-0.8); hold; the beam lifts away (1.55-2.0).

shots.line: Rule three. Don't cover them.
shots.scene: Rule card: RULE 3 / DON'T COVER THEM, progress 3 of 4.
shots.purpose: State rule three.
shots.visual_change: Hard cut to the card; rule 3 lit.

shots.line: Tape feels
shots.scene: Hypothetical begins: the frame gets a dashed border, a faint red veil and a red IF YOU COVER THEM banner. The seated person stands up at the door.
shots.purpose: Make the start of the 'what if' unmistakable.
shots.visual_change: Banner and border drop in (0-0.25); sit -> stand.

shots.line: like the right idea.
shots.scene: Hypothetical insert of the inner door face: a hand presses an opaque gray tape patch over the old lens, then a second over the new lens. Both patches stay.
shots.purpose: Show the tape making contact with and covering both openings.
shots.visual_change: Tape 1 contact at 0.32 s (old lens), tape 2 contact at 1.12 s (new lens); the hand withdraws each time.

shots.line: It isn't. Cover both, and it doesn't stop looking. It just finds somewhere closer to look from.
shots.scene: Hypothetical wide: both holes taped. The person sits back down. Pressure pulses behind the new tape; the picture on the wall begins to shake.
shots.purpose: First consequence of covering.
shots.visual_change: Sit (0.4-1.0); red pulse at the new tape (2.8-3.5); picture shake ramps (4.1-5.6).

shots.line: The picture on your wall has hung there for years. It has never had a hole in it. It does now.
shots.scene: Insert of the same framed picture (hill line and sun) with a slow push-in. On 'does' a brass eye punches through its centre with cracks and a red pulse.
shots.purpose: Reveal the escalation in a readable insert.
shots.visual_change: Still picture -> brass eye pops through at 5.37 s -> red ring.

shots.line: And from there, it can see exactly where you're sitting.
shots.scene: Back to the wide: tape on both door holes, a brass eye in the picture. A red sight-line from the picture reaches straight into the blind spot and locks on the sitting person, who flinches.
shots.purpose: Show that covering the holes destroys the blind spot.
shots.visual_change: Red line grows on 'see', locks on 'exactly', flinch on 'sitting'.

shots.line: Two holes you know about are safer than one you don't.
shots.scene: Return to reality: a white wipe travels from the door to the left edge. Behind it the tape, the picture eye, the red line, the border and the banner are gone; the person sits safe under two dark holes. Check on 'safer'.
shots.purpose: Clearly end the hypothetical and return to the main situation.
shots.visual_change: Wipe 0.03-0.75 erases the hypothetical state; status 02:47 AM; green check near the holes on 'safer'.

shots.line: Rule four. Wait for the light.
shots.scene: Rule card: RULE 4 / WAIT FOR THE LIGHT, progress 4 of 4.
shots.purpose: State rule four.
shots.visual_change: Hard cut to the card; rule 4 lit.

shots.line: Some time before morning, the hallway light will come back through the old one.
shots.scene: Insert of the inner door face, both lenses dark; the old lens fills with warm hallway light and rays.
shots.purpose: Show the old lens admitting light again.
shots.visual_change: Old lens dark -> lit with rays on 'old one' (84.28).

shots.line: It will land on your floor, right where it always does.
shots.scene: Wide: the beam draws from the old hole down to the floor, and the light spot returns to its established place; a yellow pulse marks it.
shots.purpose: Apparent safety, recognised by the returning floor light.
shots.visual_change: Beam grows (85.25-85.9), spot appears, pulse on 'always' (87.08).

shots.line: And the new one will be gone.
shots.scene: Insert of the inner door face: the lit old lens below; the brass lens above shrinks, closes and the door surface heals over it.
shots.purpose: Show the extra lens disappearing unmistakably.
shots.visual_change: Brass lens scales to zero (89.0-89.45) on 'gone'; a fading ring; status ONE PEEPHOLE.

shots.line: That means it has let go of the door. Before you get up,
shots.scene: Wide: one peephole, the floor light in its place. The person leans toward the light.
shots.purpose: Apparent relief before the final check.
shots.visual_change: Hold; lean on 'Before you get up' (92.36).

shots.line: look at the light. If it's only light, you can go to bed. If something is standing in it… it
shots.scene: Top-down insert of the warm floor spot on dark boards, the door at the right. A green check first. On 'standing', two dark feet and a long body-shaped shadow appear inside the light. In the pause one foot steps toward the door.
shots.purpose: Make the final threat concrete and specific.
shots.visual_change: Clean spot + check -> feet and shadow fade in on 'standing' -> one foot steps at 6.6 s.

shots.line: didn't go back outside. It came IN.
shots.scene: Final wide: two dark legs stand in the old beam, warm-lit at the edges. On 'came' a tall faceless silhouette resolves above them, taller than the door, with one yellow eye glint. The person recoils on 'IN'. The figure takes one slow step toward them; its shadow slides across the floor light. Hold.
shots.purpose: Payoff: something is physically inside the room.
shots.visual_change: Legs in the beam -> full silhouette (2.26-2.75) -> person recoils (2.74) -> one step (4.4-5.2) -> hold and fade.
